source_fence_representation.representation: The original required_function_order receives ['fn ', '<complete name, signature and stripped body>']; generic read_response uses the original required_order.
source_fence_representation.limitation: This fixes stripped code, not every raw source byte. String/comment contents are masked. Raw required markers are mere file-wide substrings and are not equivalent to a function-scoped literal proof.

qa_review.membership: Uses original complete _source_files collection, original Rust and cfg(test) stripping, exact product_callers equality, original _verify_boundary, adds an unexpected caller and removes each of three admitted Artifact files; also asserts Root ordinary stage assembly remains empty and authority fields remain false.
negative_categories: lost consuming continuation or unsigned precondition
service purpose/nonce or unresolved status changes
registry original writer or channel restoration bypass
readback signing or merging changed observations
qa_review.author_reported_execution: Evaluation reported nine baseline rows and 21 mutation methods (eight Selection, thirteen Artifact) passed. This review does not turn that report into independent execution evidence; the two full Rust membership methods were not executed in the author's reduced local source directory.

finding.evidence: Original stripper replaces literal contents by same-width whitespace; a same-length directory or format-literal change leaves the complete stripped body identical. This row has no raw required markers for these literals. This is a static derivation; no mutation was executed by this reviewer.
finding.effect: The v3 rules should not be described as fully fixing the original physical path namespace or file-name templates.
finding.authorized_followup: Root asked the sole CALLERS/QA writer to prepare v3.1 using unchanged verifier and Rust, retain v3 unchanged, and record actual same-length mutations.

original_literal_calls_scope.validation: Within the uniquely selected actual function, an exact source marker must have a span whose masked body equals _strip_rust_non_code(marker); exactly one actual call is required. Comments, literal contents, cfg(test) and nested-function placeholders cannot satisfy that check.
original_literal_calls_scope.placement: Include literal markers in an appropriate function-local sequence near the actual physical path/read anchors and retain the complete stripped body.
original_literal_calls_scope.reachability_limit: The original helper does not generally prove runtime reachability. The existing complete stripped body and forbidden guard entries reject insertion of a new dead branch in the approved function.
original_literal_calls_scope.format_limit: File-level required can be satisfied by a comment or unrelated raw text. A format! raw marker must not be presented as an equivalent anti-decoy function-scoped guarantee.
